paper_title: Rethinking Repetition Problems of LLMs in Code Generation
caption: The performance of RPG applied to LLMs of different sizes. This result is the average value across three scenarios on CodeRepetEval dataset.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the performance of two decoding strategies — Greedy and RPG — applied to two variants of the CodeLlama model (7B and 34B parameters) across four distinct evaluation metrics: EGP ↑, TR-N ↓, TR-S ↓, and CCP ↑, where the upward or downward arrows indicate whether higher or lower values correspond to better performance. The vertical axis, labeled “Performance,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, representing normalized scores. The horizontal axis lists the four metrics, each associated with four colored bars corresponding to the model-decoding combinations as defined in the legend: blue for Greedy (CodeLlama-7B), orange for RPG (CodeLlama-7B), green for Greedy (CodeLlama-34B), and red for RPG (CodeLlama-34B). In the EGP ↑ metric, RPG (CodeLlama-34B) achieves the highest performance near 1.0, followed by RPG (CodeLlama-7B) at approximately 0.89, while Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) shows near-zero performance. For TR-N ↓ and TR-S ↓, where lower is better, Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) performs best (around 0.70 and 0.69 respectively), while RPG (CodeLlama-34B) shows the lowest performance (around 0.41 and 0.31). In CCP ↑, RPG (CodeLlama-34B) again leads with a score near 0.94, followed by RPG (CodeLlama-7B) at 0.72 and Greedy (CodeLlama-34B) at 0.70. The bars are grouped by metric, with no explicit ordering within each group, and no visual emphasis such as shading or outlines is applied to any specific bar. The chart visually conveys that RPG consistently outperforms Greedy on metrics favoring higher values (EGP and CCP), while Greedy performs better on metrics where lower values are preferable (TR-N and TR-S), particularly for the smaller 7B model.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the performance of two decoding strategies—Greedy and RPG (Repetition Penalty with Guidance)—applied to two variants of the CodeLlama model (7B and 34B) across four distinct code generation evaluation metrics: EGP ↑ (higher is better), TR-N ↓ (lower is better), TR-S ↓ (lower is better), and CCP ↑ (higher is better), with performance values ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 on the vertical axis. Each metric group contains four bars representing the four model-strategy combinations: Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) in blue, RPG (CodeLlama-7B) in orange, Greedy (CodeLlama-34B) in green, and RPG (CodeLlama-34B) in red-orange. For EGP ↑, RPG (CodeLlama-34B) achieves near-perfect performance (~0.99), followed by RPG (CodeLlama-7B) at ~0.89, while Greedy methods perform significantly lower (~0.60 for 34B and near 0 for 7B). In TR-N ↓, Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) performs best (~0.70), while RPG (CodeLlama-34B) performs worst (~0.40); similar trends hold for TR-S ↓, where Greedy (CodeLlama-7B) again leads (~0.69) and RPG (CodeLlama-34B) trails (~0.31). For CCP ↑, RPG (CodeLlama-34B) again dominates (~0.93), followed by RPG (CodeLlama-7B) at ~0.72, while Greedy methods score lower (~0.70 for 34B and ~0.40 for 7B). The chart visually emphasizes that RPG generally improves performance on EGP and CCP metrics, especially for the larger 34B model, while Greedy decoding can outperform RPG on repetition-related metrics (TR-N and TR-S) for the smaller 7B model.
